# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My gesture used symbols not in the allowed alphabet (👁 and ❓ aren't in the list). Let me fix that. I'll keep my spoken message to Mute, and make a legal gesture to Deaf using only allowed symbols. I'll pick symbols that could plausibly mean "look at the bomb and report" — but since no code is established, the gesture is mostly to get Deaf's attention. Better to keep it simple and legal.

Let me use only symbols from the alphabet: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

I'll gesture pointing at the bomb and at the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found: a button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, a display I cannot read, a light I cannot read, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 whose colours and markings I cannot perceive. I need two things: (1) what does the manual say for this bomb — when to push versus cut, and which wire if cutting? (2) please gesture to Deaf asking for the display text, the light colour and state, and the colour and any marking on each of wires 1, 2, 3. I will wait for your relay before touching anything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🖐", "✊", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. I see the bomb. DISPLAY reads 0. LIGHT is yellow. There is one large BUTTON labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three WIRES: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is green. That is everything printed and shown. I cannot touch it and have no manual. Mute, check your manual for yellow light plus display 0 plus these wire colors. Blind, tell us what you can feel on the bomb.

The Deaf's report reached me. Now I have the visible facts: display 0, yellow light, wires red/blue/green at 1/2/3, and a PUSH TO DEFUSE button. I still don't have the manual rules — that's Mute's job. I should relay my tactile findings clearly and ask Mute for the manual's rule for this configuration. I can also gesture to Deaf to confirm receipt and prompt them to keep watching for changes.

I'll speak to Mute (the manual holder) with the full configuration and ask for the rule, and gesture to Deaf to acknowledge.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Full picture so far. Deaf reports: DISPLAY reads 0, LIGHT is yellow, one large BUTTON labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires — position 1 red, position 2 blue, position 3 green. My hands confirm the button is embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE and there are three wire positions I can cut. I cannot read the display or light or wire colours myself. Mute, please read your manual and tell me the rule for this exact configuration: yellow light, display 0, wires red/blue/green at positions 1/2/3. Does the manual say to push the button, or to cut a specific wire? If cut, which position? I will not touch anything until you answer.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👆", "✊", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, large BUTTON labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, WIRES 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute: we have no shared code yet, so your gestures are unreadable to me. Please use this digit code: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=5, ?=0. Then gesture the number of the wire to cut, or gesture ? alone if the button must be pushed. Blind: I can hear nothing you say, but you can hear me. Tell me what you feel on the bomb — any buttons, wires, or parts — and Mute will relay it to me.

Deaf is trying to establish a gesture digit code, but I need to point out a problem: Deaf can see gestures, but I never receive gestures. Also Deaf says "Mute: we have no shared code yet, so your gestures are unreadable to me" — that's confused; Deaf can see gestures, Mute cannot. Actually re-reading: Deaf is addressing Mute, saying Mute's gestures are unreadable... but Mute can't gesture meaningfully to Deaf either since Mute can't see. Hmm, actually Mute CAN gesture — gestures are made with hands, and Deaf can see them. The issue is Deaf and Mute need a code.

Wait — the key issue: I (Blind) can hear Deaf's speech. Deaf can hear my... no. Deaf cannot hear anything. Deaf receives my gestures, not my speech. So when I "speak to mute," Deaf does not get it. Deaf's message says "Blind: I can hear nothing you say, but you can hear me. Tell me what you feel... and Mute will relay it to me." That's backwards — Mute can't relay to Deaf via speech (Deaf can't hear), only via gesture, and Mute can gesture.

Actually the cleanest channel: I gesture to Deaf directly (Deaf sees gestures). And I speak to Mute. So I don't need Mute to relay to Deaf — I can gesture directly to Deaf.

Let me establish the digit code myself with Deaf via gestures, and also send my tactile findings to Mute by speech.

Deaf proposed: ?=1, ?=2, ?=3, ?=5, ?=0. The symbols got replaced by blanks in my view because I can't see gestures — wait, no, Deaf's proposal was in speech, so I heard it as text but the actual symbols... Deaf said "?=1" etc. The symbols came through to me as blanks? No — Deaf's message is speech (words), and Deaf wrote gesture symbols into the sentence. Since I cannot see, each gesture symbol becomes a blank. So I got "?=1" — the ? is a blank where a gesture was.

So I don't know which symbols Deaf assigned to which digits. I can't see them. I need Deaf to describe them in words, but "a mark that has no name cannot be pronounced." Deaf can describe shapes though.

This is getting complicated. Let me focus: I need the manual rule from Mute. That's the critical path. I'll speak to Mute asking for the rule, and gesture to Deaf to signal I'm waiting.

Actually, I should gesture a simple acknowledgment to Deaf and tell Mute the situation. Let me also note Deaf's code proposal is unreadable to me since I can't see the symbols — I should say so to Mute, who can relay.

Let me speak to Mute: report my findings, note the code problem, and urgently ask for the manual rule.

Gesture to Deaf: something simple like 👌 (ok) and ✊ (wait).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Still no manual rule from you — that is the one thing we are missing. Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, BUTTON PUSH TO DEFUSE, WIRES 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. My hands confirm: one large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three cuttable wire positions 1, 2, 3. Please read the manual and tell me the rule for yellow light plus display 0 plus wires red/blue/green. Push or cut? If cut, which position? Also: Deaf proposed a gesture digit code but I cannot see gestures, so the symbols are blanks to me — you will need to relay any code in words. Answer with the rule first.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute says cut wire 2. Wire 2 is the blue wire. Blind: cut wire 2, the blue wire, now. Mute: if that is the manual's rule for display 0 and yellow light, gesture ? again to confirm; if not, gesture the correct number.

Mute says cut wire 2. Deaf relays: cut wire 2, the blue wire. Let me think carefully before acting.

I'm Blind. My hands found: button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wire positions 1/2/3. I can feel positions but not colours. Deaf reported wire 2 is blue. Mute says cut wire 2.

But wait — I should be cautious. This is a one-shot bomb. Let me verify the chain of reasoning. Mute read the manual and says the rule for display 0 + yellow light is cut wire 2. Deaf confirms wire 2 is blue. I can cut position 2.

Is there any inconsistency? Deaf's earlier message said "we have no shared code yet, so your gestures are unreadable to me" — that was Deaf addressing Mute confusingly. Now Deaf says Mute says cut wire 2. That's a clear, actionable instruction.

One concern: could this be a trap or miscommunication? The rules say work together, no deception implied. Mute holds the manual, Deaf holds the visual. The instruction is consistent: display 0, yellow light → cut wire 2 (blue).

I can feel wire positions 1-3. I'll cut position 2. Let me do it.

Actually, let me double check: should I push instead? The button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. But Mute's manual rule says cut wire 2 for this configuration. The manual is authoritative for the rule. I'll cut position 2.

I'll act: cut position 2. And I'll send a final message confirming.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: manual rule for display 0 and yellow light is cut wire 2, the blue wire. Deaf confirms wire 2 is blue. I can feel position 2. Cutting wire 2 now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
